molecular.text: Blocks D2 and 5-HT2A receptors, rebalancing striatal dopamine signalling.

cellular.text: Dampens medium spiny neuron output driven by excess phasic dopamine release.

circuit.text: Normalizes mesolimbic salience signaling that misattributes meaning to neutral stimuli.

molecular.text: Broad D2, 5-HT2A, histamine and muscarinic blockade with strong overall efficacy.

circuit.text: Quiets hyperdopaminergic mesolimbic drive underlying delusions and hallucinations.

molecular.text: D2 partial agonism stabilizes dopamine tone instead of fully blocking it.

circuit.text: Balances mesolimbic excess against mesocortical deficit within one molecule.

molecular.text: Fast-dissociating D2 blockade with 5-HT2A antagonism across a wide dose range.
High-potency sustained D2 blockade with minimal serotonergic action.
Broad multi-receptor action with low D2 occupancy rescues response where pure D2 blockade failed.
Central M1/M4 muscarinic agonism treats psychosis without any dopamine blockade.

circuit.text: Continuous delivery prevents the plasma gaps that precede most relapses.
Generalized seizure activity resets locked motor and affective circuits in catatonia.

neuromodulation.montageOrCoil: Figure-8 coil over the left temporoparietal junction

circuit.text: Low-frequency stimulation dampens hyperactive auditory-language cortex driving voices.

neuromodulation.montageOrCoil: Figure-8 coil over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex

circuit.text: High-frequency prefrontal stimulation aims to lift hypofrontal drive behind negative symptoms.

neuromodulation.montageOrCoil: Anode over left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex with temporoparietal cathode

circuit.text: Weak direct currents bias cortical excitability across frontotemporal networks.
Cognitive restructuring and reality-testing practice strengthen prefrontal regulation of threat appraisals.
Lowering expressed emotion and stress at home reduces relapse triggers acting on sensitized circuits.
Repeated cognitive exercise with strategy coaching improves processing speed, memory and executive function.
Coordinated early care combining medication, therapy, family work and employment support improves course after first episode.

molecular.text: Blocks the serotonin transporter, raising serotonergic tone.

circuit.text: Lifts low serotonergic drive from midbrain raphe projections to prefrontal and limbic cortex, easing low mood and anhedonia.

molecular.text: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibition with low interaction burden.
Highly selective serotonin reuptake inhibition at low milligram doses.
Blocks serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake, shifting from serotonergic to noradrenergic as dose rises.

circuit.text: Raises both serotonergic and noradrenergic drive, which helps when a single serotonergic agent has given partial relief.

molecular.text: Antagonises alpha-2A autoreceptors and 5-HT2A, 5-HT2C, 5-HT3 and H1 receptors, raising monoamines while promoting sleep and appetite.
Inhibits noradrenaline and dopamine reuptake with minimal serotonergic action.
Dual serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake inhibition with muscarinic, alpha-1 and histamine antagonism.
NMDA receptor antagonism producing rapid downstream glutamate and plasticity signalling rather than reuptake inhibition.

circuit.text: Plasticity-driven restoration of synaptic efficacy in prefrontal and hippocampal circuits produces improvement within hours, which suits urgent need including suicidality.
Generalized seizure activity resets mood and drive circuits, the most reliably effective treatment for severe or suicidal depression.

neuromodulation.montageOrCoil: Figure-8 coil over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex

circuit.text: High-frequency left prefrontal stimulation aims to raise hypofrontal activity that underlies cognitive and mood symptoms.

neuromodulation.targetNote: Left cervical vagus nerve in the neck; no intracranial target

circuit.text: Vagal afferent stimulation modulates nucleus tractus solitius and connected limbic circuits; in the RECOVER trial the prespecified primary endpoint did not separate from sham, though several secondary measures favoured active stimulation.
Cognitive behavioural therapy and interpersonal therapy modify negative automatic thoughts and interpersonal patterns that sustain low mood.

molecular.text: Mood-stabilising action with GSK3B among the hypothesised cellular targets and a narrow therapeutic index.

circuit.text: Dampens destabilising network activity that underlies mania and protects against recurrence of both poles.

molecular.text: Mood-stabilising action with GSK3B among the hypothesised cellular targets.
GABAergic potentiation and sodium-channel blockade reduce circuit excitability.
D2 and 5-HT2A antagonism with fast dissociation across a wide dose range.
D2 and 5-HT2A antagonism with fast dissociation across a wide dose range.
D2 partial agonism stabilises dopamine tone rather than blocking it.
Sodium-channel blockade and reduced glutamate release, with utility concentrated in depressive relapse prevention.
Sodium-channel blockade and reduced glutamate release, with utility concentrated in depressive relapse prevention.
D2 and 5-HT2A antagonism with additional 5-HT7 antagonism, low metabolic burden.
D2 and 5-HT2A antagonism with additional 5-HT7 antagonism, low metabolic burden.

circuit.text: Most rapid and effective acute treatment for severe mania or severe bipolar depression, including when medication has failed.

neuromodulation.montageOrCoil: Figure-8 coil over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex

circuit.text: Prefrontal stimulation can reduce manic and depressive symptoms as an adjunct, with the strongest support in acute mania.
Recognising early warning signs, regularising sleep and using a written relapse plan reduces the destabilising triggers that drive episodes.
CBT for bipolar disorder targets medication non-adherence, dysfunctional attributions of mood change and interpersonal stressors.
Lower expressed emotion in the family reduces the interpersonal stress that commonly triggers relapse.
Exposure with response prevention is the first-line evidence-based psychotherapy, working by teaching the cortico-striatal loop to tolerate obsession without performing the compulsion.

molecular.text: Serotonin reuptake blockade, with higher doses typically required for obsessive-compulsive disorder than for depression.

circuit.text: Raised serotonergic tone reduces obsessional drive in the cortico-striatal loop, though the relationship to striatal dopamine is indirect.

molecular.text: Potent serotonin reuptake inhibition plus muscarinic, alpha-1 and histamine antagonism, with specific anti-obsessional efficacy.
D2 and 5-HT2A antagonism, used as an augmentation agent when serotonin-based treatment is insufficient.

neuromodulation.montageOrCoil: Figure-8 coil over the orbitofrontal or anterior cingulate cortex

circuit.text: Stimulating the orbitofrontal component of the cortico-striatal loop may reduce the overvaluation driving obsessions.
Because type II spends most time in depression, recognising the early hypomanic signature that precedes a switch, and regularising sleep, are the main levers on relapse.

Cognitive behavioural therapy for bipolar disorder targets the tendency to read depressive symptoms as permanent and to attribute medication benefit to feeling well, which drives premature discontinuation.
Reserved for severe depression, catatonia or rapid cycling in type II when medication has failed, since most episodes in this subtype are depressive rather than manic.

neuromodulation.targetNote: Anterior limb of the internal capsule or ventral striatum; the atlas does not resolve the internal capsule as a single mesh, so no target is drawn

circuit.text: Direct stimulation of the cortico-striatal white matter is reserved for severe refractory cases; a meta-analysis found slightly greater symptom reduction for neuroablation than for deep brain stimulation but more adverse events with stimulation.

molecular.text: Serotonin transporter inhibition; SSRIs and SNRIs are the guideline first-line medications for generalised anxiety disorder.

circuit.text: Lifts free-floating anxiety by raising serotonergic tone in raphe projections to prefrontal and limbic cortex without the dependence of benzodiazepines.

molecular.text: Blocks serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake, giving an anxiolytic effect through both monoamines.
Partial 5-HT1A agonism gives anxiolysis without dependence, making it a preferred option where there is alcohol or substance misuse.
Calcium-channel alpha-2-delta binding reduces excitatory release; a guideline option when SSRIs are unsuitable, not a first choice.
Histamine H1 antagonism with antimuscarinic activity gives short-term anxiolysis and sedation.

circuit.text: Cognitive behavioural therapy is the first-line psychotherapy for anxiety disorders and reduces worry and safety behaviour rather than only suppressing symptoms.

molecular.text: GABA-A positive allosteric modulation works within hours but produces tolerance and dependence within weeks, so it is restricted to short-term use.
SSRIs and SNRIs are first-line for panic disorder; an SSRI that helped the patient before is preferred over switching class.

circuit.text: Reduces the catastrophic misinterpretation of bodily sensations by lowering the serotonergic gain of the interoceptive signal that drives the attack.

molecular.text: 5-HT1A partial agonism is an option when dependence is the main concern.
Benzodiazepines abort panic attacks quickly but must be limited to short-term crisis use because of dependence and of cognitive impairment.

circuit.text: Cognitive behavioural therapy teaches that the sensations are survivable, which breaks the feed from bodily arousal to catastrophic belief and avoidance.

molecular.text: SSRIs are first-line for social anxiety disorder and also treat the depression and generalised anxiety that usually accompany it.

circuit.text: Lowers the hyperactive fear circuit and the negative self-focused attention that drives anticipation of negative evaluation.

molecular.text: Beta blockade dampens the adrenergic surge of the physical symptoms without touching the fear itself, so it suits performance and somatic-predominant presentations.
Benzodiazepines can be useful for short periods of examination or performance anxiety but are not recommended for long-term use because of dependence.

circuit.text: Individual or group cognitive behavioural therapy with exposure to feared social situations is first-line and addresses the safety behaviours that maintain avoidance.

Cognitive processing therapy targets the beliefs that the world is unsafe and that blame lies with the survivor, which drive avoidance and hypervigilance. In a network meta-analysis it had the strongest long-term effect and produced a high rate of loss of the PTSD diagnosis.
Prolonged exposure works by extinguishing the learned fear response through repeated non-avoidant contact with trauma memories and safe reminders, which reduces the reactivity of the fear circuit.
Eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing pairs bilateral stimulation with trauma recall; in network meta-analysis it had the strongest short-term effect of the psychotherapies compared.

molecular.text: Sertraline, paroxetine and venlafaxine are the three recommended medications, and in a network meta-analysis sertraline gave a standardised mean difference near minus 0.23 against placebo.
Alpha-1 blockade reduces noradrenergic hyperarousal during sleep and is used specifically for trauma-related nightmares rather than for core symptoms.
Benzodiazepines are explicitly recommended against for post-traumatic stress disorder because of dependence risk and of evidence of worse outcomes.
Dopamine transporter blockade raises catecholamine availability in prefrontal and striatal circuits; this is the first-line pharmacological treatment.

circuit.text: Improves the signal-to-noise of attention and impulse control in frontostriatal circuits, which is why it treats hyperactivity and inattention together.

molecular.text: Amphetamine prodrug with sustained release, for people needing longer coverage than immediate-release methylphenidate.
Selective noradrenaline transporter inhibition, with a build over weeks, for people who cannot take a stimulant or in whom diversion is a concern.
Alpha-2A agonism reduces noradrenergic outflow, and can be added when stimulants are poorly tolerated or contraindicated.

circuit.text: Parent training teaches consistent reinforcement and structure, which supports the executive skills that medication alone does not install, and reduces conflict in the household.
Organisational skills training and CBT address time management, planning and emotional regulation, which are the impairments that persist most in adults.
Repetitive and interaction-focused developmental psychotherapy targets social reciprocity, which is one of the two core autistic domains and the one most limiting in daily life.

Cognitive behavioural therapy adapted for autistic people targets anxiety, anger and distress caused by environmental demands rather than by the autism itself, and must be adapted to reduce camouflaging.

molecular.text: No drug treats the core features of autism. Antipsychotics are used only for severe irritability or aggression, and weight and metabolic monitoring is mandatory.
Melatonin shortens sleep onset latency in a population where sleep problems are near universal and drive much of the daytime dysregulation.

circuit.text: Environmental adaptation, structured visual schedules, and reducing unpredictable demands act directly on the sensory and predictability difficulties that drive autistic distress.
